summary: Sanders County, MT lookout 2 mi NE of Agency, filed under the National Bison Range; 1930s steel tower (72 ft), now gone.

facts.status_note: firelookout.com lists it as gone; the Forest Lookouts page marks it removed; no removal date in the sources read
facts.agency: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (National Bison Range)

events.note: firelookout.com dates the 72-foot steel tower to the 1930s; no exact year given
Forest Lookouts page marks the site Removed; no year given

evidence.supports: tower built in the 1930s, 72 feet, steel, now gone
site filed under the National Bison Range, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service
evidence.quote: National Bison Range - U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service

evidence.supports: crew of 25 men employed on the range with road construction and erecting three 60-foot steel towers for lookout fire stations
evidence.quote: A crew of 25 men are employed on the Bison range with road construction

evidence.supports: three 60-foot steel towers for lookout fire stations
evidence.quote: erection of three 60-foot steel towers for lookout fire stations

evidence.supports: report names High Point, Wild Horse Mesa and Thumb-Nob as the sites
evidence.quote: They are to be located at High Point, Wild Horse Mesa, and Thumb-Nob.

evidence.supports: listed as a tower, status gone, Sanders County
range formerly called the National Bison Range
evidence.quote: Formerly called the National Bison Range

evidence.quote: Management of the site was transferred back to the Confederated Salish and Kootenai Tribes (CSKT) in 2022 from the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service

evidence.quote: The BR has a visitor center, and two scenic roads that allow vehicular access to prime viewing areas.

corrections.why: firelookout.com gives a 72-foot steel tower (about 21.9 m); 18.3 m is 60 feet, the height in a 1934 report that names three other sites rather than this one

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com gives 72 feet. The 60-foot towers in the 1934 report are placed at High Point, Wild Horse Mesa and Thumb-Nob, not Headquarters Ridge, so the report does not settle this tower's height. The story uses 72 feet and says so.

sources.title: Headquarters Ridge
sources.publisher: Montana Forest Lookouts (Rex's Fire Lookout Page)

notes_for_editor: Access key omitted: no source describes access to this spot. Wikipedia describes the range's visitor center and scenic roads, not this site. No staffing, fire or removal-date sources found. The Wild Horse page on the same range carries the same 1934 quote (search snippet), so the Forest Lookouts page's link of that quote to this site is weak. Two web searches used.
